$schema_note: MTower Studio — recipe for an actor's LoRA training set. Each variation is one reference edit of the approved anchor (same person, new angle, light, expression, pose, or outfit). 'caption' is written next to the image for training and describes only what changes (pose, light, clothing, setting), never the face, so the face binds to the trigger word. 'outfit'/'outfit_female' put the person in new clothes (named in the edit and the caption); variations without an outfit keep the anchor clothes, and their caption names the actor's anchor.outfit. Rule (v1.2): at least 3 out of 4 variations change the outfit and at least 4 are action poses, so neither the anchor clothes nor the portrait framing become part of the face. Optional 'edit_female'/'caption_female' replace the text for female actors. Used by: mtower generate training-set <ACT-ID>.
identity_lock: Keep exactly the same person: the same face, facial features, face shape, nose, eyes, eyebrows, skin tone, age, build, hair and facial hair. If the person wears a headscarf, keep the hair covered. Photorealistic 35mm film photograph, natural unretouched skin texture, 1970s Egypt, no text or lettering anywhere.

gate.$note: Checked before every paid LoRA training run (mtower generate lora). Prevents training on a set that would bake the anchor clothes or portrait framing into the face.

child_safe.$note: Actors with apparent_age < 16: these variations are skipped (undershirts / soaked clinging clothes are not suitable training images of a child, and Azure's safety filter rejects them). 'carrying' (a child straining under a load) trips Azure vision filters even fully clothed (2026-10-18).
